jobs.description: Evolve have partnered with a leading Ophthalmology organisation who are looking for a Regional Sales Manager to join their team within their Retail Optics division. This is an exciting opportunity to lead and develop a high-performing sales team while driving regional growth and building strong relationships with key customers. With a strong focus on coaching and field leadership, this role offers the chance to make a real commercial impact within a dynamic and growing business. This is a full-time permanent position covering the North of the UK. What’s on offer? Excellent Salary & Benefits - A competitive starting salary depending on experience, plus exceptional bonus, company car, car allowance, pension, healthcare and more! Innovative Product Portfolio - Work with a leading retail optic product range in a specialist market. Collaborative Culture - Thrive in a supportive, people-focused environment. Ideal Requirements for the Regional Sales Manager Experience in Life Sciences, Pharmaceuticals, or Medical Device - A solid background within life sciences, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, or a related commercial environment, bringing valuable industry insight and credibility with healthcare customers. Proven Leadership in Sales Management - Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing sales teams, with the ability to inspire, coach, and motivate individuals to consistently achieve ambitious regional targets. jobs.description: Location: Home-based, covering a national UK territory Products and services: Temperature and humidity monitoring systems, UKAS-accredited calibration, temperature mapping and validation Customers: Medical, healthcare, pharmaceutical, laboratory, warehousing and cold-chain distribution organisations Who you'll be working for Tek-Troniks is a privately owned British manufacturer with over 30 years’ experience in temperature and humidity monitoring, calibration and validation. Its products and services help customers protect temperature-sensitive materials, maintain accurate records and demonstrate regulatory compliance. The company designs and manufactures its products in the UK, combining established technical capabilities with the accessible management structure of a small business. It already supplies regulated organisations, including NHS customers, pharmaceutical businesses and distribution facilities, and is now appointing a dedicated national salesperson to develop these markets. Why should you join? Freedom to manage your territory: You’ll decide where to focus your efforts and when customer visits, demonstrations or remote meetings will best move an opportunity forward. Performance is measured through commercial results, with no prescribed weekly field-visit target. An established proposition with room to grow: You’ll represent proven products and services in markets where the company already has customers, with considerable scope to develop new relationships and opportunities. Uncapped earning potential: The commission scheme rewards both new business and qualifying repeat revenue from accounts you originate, allowing you to benefit from the relationships you build. A voice in the business: Working closely with senior management, you’ll help shape market priorities, sales processes and marketing activity, while feeding customer insight into future product development. Technical support and training: You’ll learn from the General Manager and work directly with colleagues in engineering, calibration, internal sales and production. What the role involves You’ll take ownership of new business development across the UK, selling an integrated range of monitoring systems, calibration and mapping services into regulated environments. This is a consultative sales role, helping customers understand how the company’s solutions can meet their operational and compliance requirements. Your responsibilities will include: Identifying and approaching prospective customers across healthcare, pharmaceuticals, laboratories and regulated distribution. Building relationships with technical, quality, compliance and purchasing stakeholders. Understanding customer requirements, arranging demonstrations and preparing appropriate proposals and quotations. Managing opportunities from initial enquiry through to negotiation and sale. Developing accounts beyond the first installation, including opportunities across additional sites. Assessing relevant public-sector tenders and other routes to market. Maintaining a sustainable pipeline and contributing ideas to the company’s commercial approach. You’ll work from home, travelling nationally when required, with occasional overnight stays. Initial training will include approximately three to four weeks working closely with the business to develop your product and market knowledge. Person requirements You’ll have proven technical or consultative sales experience within a regulated market, together with evidence of winning new business and managing opportunities through to completion. Your background could include medical or pharmaceutical equipment, laboratory instrumentation, environmental monitoring, calibration, validation, cold-chain technology, aseptic processing or sterile services. Direct temperature monitoring experience isn’t essential if you bring relevant sector knowledge and the ability to learn a technical portfolio. You’ll also need: An understanding of quality systems, documented processes and the expectations of regulated customers. The confidence to discuss technical requirements and build credibility with specialist decision-makers. Strong prospecting, relationship-building and commercial skills. The judgement and self-motivation to manage a national territory independently. A willingness to learn, ask questions and contribute ideas as the business develops. Knowledge of GxP, MHRA or GDP requirements would be valuable. An existing network of quality or compliance contacts would also be an advantage. Basic salary: Circa £50,000–£60,000 Bonus: Uncapped commission, with £18,000 commission at the annual revenue target, plus qualifying trailing commission Car allowance: £5,000 per annum

Encouraging sustained utilisation and monitoring clinical usage, performance and outcomes. Supporting evaluations, bids and account plans alongside the wider commercial team. Sharing customer feedback and clinical insights to inform product and workflow improvements. Your requirements Experience with robotics in spinal surgery is essential for this position. You’ll bring a strong understanding of spinal procedures and the operating theatre environment, together with the confidence to support surgical teams during live cases. We’re looking for: A clinical background, such as an ODP, scrub nurse, allied health professional or equivalent. Relevant experience in spinal surgery, orthopaedics and enabling technologies, including spinal robotics. A thorough understanding of surgical workflows and the practical demands of theatre. Strong communication, presentation and training skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly. The ability to build credibility with surgeons and work effectively with multidisciplinary hospital teams. A practical approach to troubleshooting and supporting the adoption of new technology. The organisation and independence needed to manage a national, field-based role with significant travel. Basic salary: £52,000 to £61,000 Bonus: £18,000 per annum, paid quarterly Car: Company car with electric and hybrid options, or allowance options of £7,000 cash or £6,000 towards a lease per year Benefits: 25 days’ holiday, pension, healthcare, lunch allowance, laptop and a range of flexible benefits and employee discounts

jobs.title: Territory Manager - Ambulance & Post-Acute Care
jobs.description: Location: Ideally based in the South West or South Wales. The territory covers the South West, South Wales and West Midlands up to Birmingham, plus Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire, Berkshire, Hampshire and Surrey. Products: You’ll sell a focused portfolio of medical devices across ambulance, acute and community care settings: Falls recovery equipment: An established lifting chair that helps people recover safely from the floor following a fall. Customers include ambulance services, care home groups, occupational therapists and NHS manual handling teams. Non-contact thermometers: A newly introduced range listed on NHS Supply Chain and HCA frameworks, with opportunities across acute wards, paediatrics, oncology and critical care. Key contacts include clinical leads, infection control teams, clinical engineering and procurement. The role combines developing an established customer base for falls recovery equipment with winning new business for the temperature monitoring range. The company Our client is an established medical device distributor working with leading healthcare manufacturers across the UK and Ireland. Combining specialist sales expertise with clinical education and technical support, the business helps healthcare professionals introduce and use technologies that improve patient care. You’ll join its ambulance and post-acute care division, supplying practical solutions to NHS Trusts, ambulance services, care homes and community healthcare teams. With an established customer base and a newly launched product range, this is an opportunity to build on existing relationships while developing new business within a close, supportive team. Why you should join You’ll take responsibility for a growing territory with an established customer base and a newly launched product range. This gives you the opportunity to develop existing accounts while building new business across hospitals, ambulance services and care providers. The products have a practical impact on patient care, helping people recover safely after falls and supporting clinical teams with temperature monitoring. You’ll join a close, supportive team with the independence to plan your territory and take ownership of its growth. Responsibilities Grow sales, revenue and market share across the territory, achieving agreed sales and margin targets. Develop existing accounts for an established falls recovery product and win new customers for a recently launched non-contact thermometer. Build relationships with ambulance services, NHS Trusts, care home groups and community healthcare providers. Engage clinical and commercial decision-makers, including procurement, infection prevention and control, manual handling teams, occupational therapists, paramedics and clinical engineering departments. Deliver practical product demonstrations, customer training and assessments, including in patients’ homes where required. Support product evaluations and work with customers through procurement and approval processes. Maintain a territory business plan, manage your pipeline and keep customer records and sales forecasts up to date. Attend exhibitions, workshops, training and supplier meetings, including occasional overseas travel and weekend commitments. Person requirements You’ll be a self-motivated sales professional who enjoys finding opportunities, opening doors and converting interest into business. You’ll be comfortable managing a broad territory independently, while contributing to a supportive team. Ideally, you’ll bring experience selling medical devices or consumables into NHS Trusts or community services, with an understanding of NHS procurement, clinical evaluations and purchasing approvals. Driven candidates with relevant transferable sales experience will also be considered. You’ll need: Strong relationship-building, presentation and negotiation skills. The drive to win new business alongside the discipline to develop existing accounts. A warm, sensitive approach when working with vulnerable patients and their families. The ability to transport equipment and carry out practical product demonstrations safely. Good organisation, IT skills and a full driving licence. Willingness to travel throughout the territory and undertake the required DBS checks. Experience selling into ambulance services or care homes would be an advantage, as would knowledge of NHS Wales procurement and health boards. A clinical background in nursing, paramedicine or occupational therapy would also be valuable. Basic salary: £35,000 to £46,000 per annum. Bonus: £24,000 per annum, paid quarterly, combining a target-based bonus with uncapped commission, currently 2% on sales. Company car: Tesla. You’ll also receive: 25 days’ annual leave, increasing with service after five years to a maximum of 30 days. 5% employer pension contribution. Life assurance worth four times your annual salary. Permanent health insurance to support you if you’re unable to work due to illness or injury. Enhanced family leave and sick pay. Confidential 24/7 employee assistance programme for you and your household, plus access to trained Mental Health First Aiders. Funded eye tests, a contribution towards eyewear and a Cycle to Work scheme. Volunteer days, charity sponsorship support, employee events and recognition awards. Access to financial advice, retirement planning support and an employee savings scheme. £5/day lunch allowance

jobs.title: Inside Sales Executive
jobs.description: Location: Sheffield, predominantly office-based Products: Breast Care, Orthotics and Walking Aids Who you will be working for Our client is a well-established global manufacturer and distributor of healthcare products, specialising in breast care, orthotics and walking aids. Their products support patients' mobility, independence and quality of life, with customers including the NHS, private healthcare providers, specialist clinics and distributors. Due to continued growth, they are looking to recruit an Inside Sales Executive to join their Sheffield-based team, supporting sales activity across the UK. Why you should join Join an established, successful healthcare company with a strong reputation and excellent staff retention. Become part of a close-knit, friendly and supportive team where people genuinely enjoy working together. Work with an approachable manager who encourages independence, trusts her team and doesn't micromanage. Enjoy a varied role combining sales, account management, business development and market research. Receive full product training, so previous medical device or healthcare experience isn't essential. Have the opportunity to develop your commercial skills and potentially progress into a field-based sales role. Join a growing team where you can take ownership of your work and make a genuine contribution to business growth. Job responsibilities This is a varied, office-based sales position combining existing account management, proactive new business development and support for the external sales team. You will work across three product groups, breast care, orthotics and walking aids, helping to identify and develop opportunities throughout the UK. Your responsibilities will include: Proactively identifying and developing new business opportunities through telephone, email and digital engagement. Managing and developing relationships with existing customers, including NHS departments, private healthcare providers, clinics and distributors. Researching potential customers, mapping market opportunities and identifying areas for business growth. Following up sales leads, customer enquiries and marketing campaigns to convert opportunities into orders. Identifying cross-selling and upselling opportunities across the product portfolio. Supporting the external Territory Managers with prospecting, customer appointments and regional sales development. Preparing and following up quotations, pricing proposals and tender documentation. Maintaining and updating customer databases, ensuring accurate contact information and sales records. Assisting with product launches, training activities, promotional campaigns and events. Monitoring sales opportunities, tracking progress against targets and providing market and competitor intelligence. Working closely with customer service, marketing and operations to ensure customers receive a professional and responsive service. Person requirements We are looking for a proactive, commercially minded individual who enjoys speaking with customers, developing relationships and finding new business opportunities. This role would particularly suit someone in the early stages of their sales career who is keen to take on more responsibility and develop within the healthcare industry. Essential: Previous experience in an internal sales, telesales, outbound sales or customer-facing sales role, ideally with at least 1-2 years' experience. Confident telephone manner with the ability to build rapport and develop customer relationships. A proactive approach to prospecting and identifying new sales opportunities. Strong communication, organisational and administrative skills. Self-motivated, resilient and comfortable working towards sales targets. Able to work independently, use initiative and manage competing priorities. Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and Excel. Adaptable and comfortable working across different products, customers and sales approaches. Desirable: Experience within healthcare, medical devices or a related industry. Knowledge of NHS customers, procurement or tender processes. Experience preparing quotations or supporting field-based sales teams. Previous healthcare experience is not essential. More important is your enthusiasm for sales, willingness to learn and ability to take ownership of opportunities. Salary and benefits Basic salary: £27,000 - £30,000 Bonus potential: £6,000 Annual leave: 24 days plus bank holidays Pension: Company pension scheme Location: Sheffield, predominantly office-based with occasional customer travel Training: Full product training and ongoing development Career progression: Potential opportunity to move into an external sales position

jobs.title: Territory Sales Manager - Airway Management & Visualisation
jobs.description: Location: Sussex, Kent, Surrey, Hampshire & the South Coast including Dartford, Medway, Canterbury, Tunbridge, Brighton, Portsmouth, Southampton, Reading, Guildford, Redhill. You'll need to live within or close to the territory and be comfortable travelling regularly to customer sites. Products: Video laryngoscopy, bronchoscopy and airway management systems Who you'll be working for A global medical device manufacturer and recognised market leader in video laryngoscopy, providing innovative technologies that help clinicians improve patient care. The company specialises in advanced visualisation and airway management solutions, including video laryngoscopes and single-use bronchoscopes used across critical care, anaesthesia and operating theatres. With an established reputation, a growing respiratory and pulmonology portfolio and a strong commitment to product innovation, the business offers an exciting opportunity to join a successful and expanding team. Why should you join? Market-leading products: Represent the global market leader in video laryngoscopy, with an established customer base and a growing portfolio of airway management solutions. Excellent earning potential: Uncapped monthly commission with accelerators once you exceed target, providing genuine opportunities to increase your earnings. Career development: Comprehensive product training, ongoing professional development and opportunities for internal progression. Supportive team culture: Join a close-knit, collaborative team that regularly gets together for company events, celebrations and team-building activities. Employee wellbeing: A company that values work-life balance, employee engagement and wellbeing, with a comprehensive benefits package. The role As Territory Sales Manager, you'll take responsibility for developing and growing sales of a market-leading range of video laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy systems across the South East. This is a customer-facing role combining new business development with account management. You'll work closely with clinicians and hospital decision-makers, demonstrating how the company's technology can improve clinical workflows and patient care. Your responsibilities will include: Managing and developing an established territory, identifying opportunities to grow existing accounts and win new business. Building strong relationships with anaesthetists, surgeons, theatre teams, critical care clinicians, nursing staff and senior hospital decision-makers. Conducting product demonstrations, evaluations and presentations to demonstrate the clinical and commercial benefits of the portfolio. Identifying new business opportunities through proactive prospecting and regular face-to-face customer engagement. Managing the full sales process, from initial engagement and product evaluation through to proposals, negotiations and closing sales. Developing territory business plans, maintaining an accurate sales pipeline and working towards monthly, quarterly and annual targets. Working with clinical and commercial stakeholders to understand their challenges and provide appropriate solutions. Who we're looking for We're looking for a driven, ambitious and commercially minded individual who enjoys being out in front of customers and has the motivation to develop new business. You don't need previous airway management experience, as comprehensive product training will be provided. Ideally, you'll bring: Some field sales experience, preferably within medical devices, healthcare or another B2B environment. Experience selling into operating theatres, anaesthesia or critical care would be advantageous, but isn't essential. An understanding of capital equipment sales or experience managing product evaluations would be beneficial. Confidence building relationships with clinical and commercial decision-makers. A proactive, competitive approach to sales, with the resilience and determination to pursue new opportunities. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage your own territory, priorities and sales pipeline. Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence customers at different levels. We're also interested in hearing from people earlier in their sales careers , including Associate Sales Representatives who are ready to take on their own territory. If you're a self-starter with the drive to succeed, the company is willing to invest in your development. Salary & Benefits Basic salary: £45,000–£58,000 depending on experience. Bonus: Uncapped commission based on sales, paid monthly, with accelerators above 100% of target. Company car or car allowance: £650 per month (£7,800 annually). Pension: 4% employer contribution with 5% employee contribution through salary sacrifice. Private healthcare: AXA. Health cash plan: Simplyhealth, providing support towards dental, GP, chiropractic and other healthcare costs. Additional benefits: Paid leave, family and medical leave provisions, employee wellbeing initiatives and professional development opportunities.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager – Orthopaedic Power Tools
jobs.description: *]:pointer-events-auto R6Vx5W_threadScrollVars scroll-mb-[calc(var(--scroll-root-safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)+var(--thread-response-height))] scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-height)+min(200px,max(70px,20svh)))]" dir="auto" data-turn-id="request-6ab24ab4-2190-83eb-a302-80066ab866fc-0" data-turn-id-container="request-6ab24ab4-2190-83eb-a302-80066ab866fc-0" data-testid="conversation-turn-12" data-turn="assistant"> div:has([data-free-thinking-preview-answer=true])+:is(.text-message,.relative:has(>.text-message))]:-mt-2 grow"> Location: South Thames – BN, BR, CR, KT, PO, RH, SM, TN and TW. You’ll need to live within or close to the territory. Product: Surgical power tools and associated disposable products used across trauma, joint replacement, maxillofacial surgery, hand and foot surgery and plastics. Who you’ll be working for: A privately owned, family-run medical device manufacturer with more than 100 years of history and a global presence. The company specialises in surgical power tools and has built its reputation around world-class products backed by strong customer service. Unlike many larger orthopaedic companies, it does not manufacture implants – surgical power tools are the core of the business. The company takes a long-term approach to both its customers and its people, with fewer corporate layers, accessible senior management and considerable emphasis on personal responsibility. What you’ll enjoy: Taking genuine ownership of your own medical sales territory, with responsibility for the accounts, activity and commercial results. Inheriting existing customer relationships while having plenty of scope to develop new business. Selling a specialist product portfolio where you can develop genuine technical and clinical expertise. A mix of capital equipment sales and recurring disposable business. Working directly with surgeons, theatre teams and other healthcare professionals. The freedom to plan and manage your own diary, while still being part of an established and supportive UK sales team. Joining a growing, family-owned manufacturer with opportunities to develop your career over time. An uncapped commission scheme with existing business on the territory and no threshold before you start earning commission. What you’ll be doing: Managing and developing existing hospital accounts across the South Thames territory. Identifying and winning new business with hospitals where there is scope to increase market share. Building relationships with surgeons, ODPs, theatre managers, nursing teams, procurement and other decision-makers. Identifying capital replacement opportunities and developing them through the sales process. Carrying out product demonstrations, evaluations and user training. Preparing quotations and supporting tender activity. Developing ongoing disposable sales from customers already using the company’s systems. Planning your territory, managing your pipeline and deciding where to focus your time. Travelling regularly between hospitals and customer sites across the region. Here’s what you need: There are several backgrounds that could work well for this opportunity. You might already be in medical device sales and ready to take ownership of your own territory, or be working as a Sales Associate or Clinical Specialist and looking for greater commercial responsibility. Alternatively, you could come from a clinical background such as an ODP, scrub nurse, theatre practitioner, theatre manager or physiotherapist. There may also be potential for someone with advanced scientific or postgraduate education who is genuinely motivated to build a career in medical sales. Whatever your background, you’ll need: Strong communication and relationship-building skills. The credibility to work effectively with healthcare professionals. Commercial drive and a genuine interest in sales and new business development. The ability to organise yourself and manage a territory independently. Resilience and the confidence to deal with setbacks and changing priorities. A practical, customer-focused and can-do approach. The motivation to work towards sales targets and take responsibility for commercial results. Salary: £31,000–£39,000 depending on experience. Bonus: Uncapped commission at 1.5% of territory sales, paid monthly on the previous month’s sales. There is no threshold and existing business is already in place. Commission at the £1.55m territory target would be £23,250. Car policy: Company car. Benefits: 25 days’ holiday and 6% employer pension contribution.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager – Middle East & Africa
jobs.description: Location: UK-based, home working with extensive international travel across the Middle East and Africa. Territory excludes South Africa and Israel. To be based ideally within one hour of Aylesbury, however, they are flexible for the right person with good access to a major international airport. Product: Premium surgical power tools and associated technology used across orthopaedic and other bone surgery applications. Who you’ll be working for: A privately owned, family-run medical device manufacturer with a global presence and more than a century of heritage. This is a newly created position resulting from continued growth within the international business. You’ll inherit an established region generating approximately £2.3m in annual sales, with existing distributor relationships, account history and internal knowledge already in place. The company has a strong reputation for product quality, responsive customer service and long-term relationships. Long service is common, and people are given considerable autonomy once trust has been established. What you’ll enjoy: Taking ownership of an established multimillion-pound international region rather than starting with a blank sheet of paper. A clear growth opportunity, with a target of approximately £2.7m compared with £2.3m in sales during the previous year. Developing sales through an established network of distributors and agents across a diverse range of international markets. Considerable autonomy over your diary, travel and commercial priorities. Working for a privately owned business with a long-term approach to growth and product development. An uncapped commission scheme paid on actual sales, with no minimum threshold before you start earning commission. A structured handover from the experienced Regional Managers who currently manage these markets. What you’ll be doing: Managing and developing an existing network of distributors and agents across the Middle East and Africa. Identifying opportunities to increase market penetration and grow sales across the region. Assessing distributor performance and helping partners improve their product knowledge, sales capability and commercial activity. Identifying gaps in market coverage and, where necessary, evaluating, recruiting and onboarding new or replacement distributors. Supporting distributors with important opportunities, product demonstrations, trials and customer meetings. Building relationships with hospitals, surgeons and other end users alongside local partners. Managing capital equipment opportunities with sales cycles ranging from a matter of weeks to 6–12 months. Planning and undertaking international trips involving multiple countries, distributors and customer meetings. Preparing quotations, following up opportunities and maintaining momentum across the territory between visits. You should expect to tour the region approximately three to four times per year, with individual trips potentially lasting two to three weeks. Overall, you’re likely to spend around a quarter to a third of the year away from home. Here’s what you need: Medical device sales experience, ideally involving surgical or technically complex products. International sales or distributor/channel management experience would be advantageous, but isn't essential. Strong commercial drive and the ability to develop sales through other people. Excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple countries, partners, opportunities and travel plans. The confidence and self-sufficiency to work independently from home and while travelling internationally. Sound commercial judgement and a calm, constructive approach when plans change or problems arise. The ability and willingness to develop sufficient technical and clinical knowledge to credibly support product demonstrations, trials and customer discussions. A genuine appetite for extensive international travel. Salary: Up to approximately £50,000, dependent on experience. Bonus: 1.2% commission on sales, paid monthly in arrears. No threshold and no commission cap. Indicative first-year OTE approximately £77,800–£82,800, dependent on territory sales performance. Car policy: £7,200 annual car allowance. Benefits: 25 days' holiday, 6% employer pension contribution, company-funded flights, accommodation and reasonable meals/expenses, company credit card for appropriate travel expenditure, travel insurance and time off in lieu for bank holidays spent travelling.

jobs.title: Territory Manager – Vascular
jobs.description: Location: Scotland. This is a field-based role covering Scotland, with key accounts and opportunities across Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Golden Jubilee, Edinburgh, Dundee, Grampian/Aberdeen and surrounding referral networks. Who you'll be working for : Our client is a global medical device company specialising in devices, implants and services for the treatment of peripheral vascular disease. The business operates internationally, with products sold in more than 90 countries. Its portfolio is focused primarily on the needs of vascular surgeons and includes products used across aortic, AV access, cardiac, carotid, lower extremity and neuro applications. Despite its global reach, the company deliberately maintains an entrepreneurial, small-company culture with an emphasis on teamwork, commercial freedom and decentralised decision-making. Why you should join : This is a role for someone who wants genuine ownership of their territory rather than operating within a heavily structured corporate sales environment. Scotland already has an established customer presence, but there is considerable headroom to grow product adoption, reactivate accounts and develop new business. You will have the freedom to identify where the opportunities lie and shape your territory accordingly. You will also have access to a broad specialist portfolio rather than being restricted to a single product, creating multiple opportunities to engage customers and develop accounts. The culture particularly suits commercially driven people who enjoy autonomy, are prepared to create their own opportunities and want their individual contribution to have a visible impact on business performance. The company combines the reach of an international medical device business with a more agile, entrepreneurial working environment. What you'll be doing : This is an opportunity to take ownership of an established but underdeveloped Scotland territory with significant potential for growth. You will be responsible for developing sales and profitability across the region, strengthening existing accounts and identifying new opportunities across a broad specialist vascular portfolio. Glasgow is a particular priority and represents one of the company's largest UK centres, while there is further potential across other major Scottish accounts. This is not simply an account maintenance role. You will be expected to actively create growth by understanding individual accounts, identifying gaps in product usage, developing clinical advocates and introducing products into new areas. Key responsibilities will include: Achieving monthly, quarterly and annual sales and gross profit objectives. Developing and executing territory and individual account plans. Identifying new opportunities within existing, underdeveloped and target accounts. Building relationships with vascular surgeons, interventionalists, theatre teams, procurement and hospital purchasing stakeholders. Driving adoption of the wider product portfolio, including key growth products within vascular and surgical applications. Supporting customers in theatre and attending procedures where appropriate. Delivering product training, workshops and first-use support. Managing both clinician-led and procurement-led sales processes. Preparing customer quotations and proposals. Managing consignment stock and coordinating customer and product activity. Maintaining accurate CRM records and developing opportunities through Salesforce. Working independently across the territory while collaborating closely with the National Sales Manager and wider team. What you'll need : You will ideally be an experienced medical device sales professional who is comfortable working within surgical, theatre or procedural environments. Cardiovascular, vascular or endovascular experience would be advantageous, but is not essential. More important is your ability to develop new business, manage a territory independently and build credibility with hospital-based clinical and commercial stakeholders. You should have: Existing medical device sales experience. Experience selling products used within theatre or procedural environments. A demonstrable track record of developing business rather than simply maintaining established accounts. Confidence engaging with clinicians, theatre teams, procurement and other hospital stakeholders. Strong territory management, planning and organisational skills. A proactive, commercially curious and opportunity-led approach. The confidence to challenge customers constructively and overcome objections. The independence and resilience to operate successfully within a lean, entrepreneurial organisation. Good CRM and Microsoft Office skills. Salesforce experience would be advantageous. Willingness to travel extensively throughout Scotland. Basic salary: £50,000 Bonus/commission: Target earnings equivalent to 40% of basic salary, structured across monthly, quarterly and annual components. Monthly commission starts at 85% of sales plan, with performance capped at 225%. Quarterly bonus is capped at 100% and year-end bonus at 120% of plan. Pension: 4% employer contribution. Holiday: 25 days plus bank holidays.

jobs.title: Account Manager - Radiology
jobs.description: Location: North West/ Yorkshire (Wakefield, Hull, Yorkshire, Greater Manchester, Merseyside, Lancashire, South Cumbria, Cheshire) Product: Contrast Media & medical devices and advanced administration systems for contrast imaging products - for use in X-Ray Imaging, MRI & CT scanners Who you’ll be working for: Our client is a global healthcare organisation specialising in diagnostic imaging. With a long-established heritage and privately owned structure, the company develops, manufactures and markets contrast agents, medical devices and advanced imaging solutions used by healthcare professionals worldwide. Diagnostic imaging sits at the heart of the organisation's strategy and expertise, with leading positions across: CT contrast media MRI contrast media Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound (CEUS) Nuclear medicine Advanced imaging technologies Operating in more than 100 countries, the business continues to invest significantly in research, innovation and clinical education, supporting improvements in diagnostic pathways and patient outcomes across healthcare systems globally. What you’ll enjoy: You'll be part of a close-knit team, where everyone mucks in together. An agile business with open communication channels making it straightforward to get things done. You'll have a supportive manager, who really looks out for her team. It's an autonomous working culture with no micromanagement! Competitive package with bonus scheme which you'll be eligible for immediately. What you’ll be doing: We're looking for an Account Manager to join the company's radiology team, managing a strategically important territory covering North West England and Yorkshire. This is a highly varied role combining account management, business development, product launches and strategic territory planning. You'll work with NHS and private healthcare customers across the company's radiology portfolio, including CT contrast media, MRI contrast media, injector systems, consumables and service solutions. A key focus will be growing and protecting the company's CT injector business, supporting customers through the transition to the next-generation injector platform, driving adoption of the MRI portfolio and identifying opportunities to expand utilisation across existing and new accounts. You'll build relationships with radiologists, radiographers, procurement teams, CT leads and other key stakeholders, helping customers improve diagnostic imaging services whilst delivering sustainable commercial growth across the territory. Here’s what you need: We're interested in commercially driven individuals who can build strong customer relationships, manage complex NHS sales environments and identify opportunities for growth. Particularly relevant backgrounds include: Radiology sales. Medical imaging sales. Contrast media sales. Capital equipment sales. Clinical specialist or applications specialist roles with commercial exposure. Radiography, particularly CT or MRI experience. Experience selling into radiology departments, knowledge of NHS procurement and tendering processes, and familiarity with MRI, CT imaging or imaging devices would be highly advantageous. You will also ideally have: Experience within healthcare, medical devices, pharmaceuticals or diagnostic imaging sales. Strong account management and business development experience. Experience managing NHS sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders. A proven track record of achieving sales targets and growing accounts. Excellent territory planning and organisational skills. Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management abilities. We're looking for someone with a strong work ethic who enjoys building long-term relationships, works well autonomously and thrives within a collaborative team environment. You'll be commercially minded, proactive, resilient and motivated by the opportunity to develop a strategically important territory. Salary: c£56,000 Bonus : c£15,000 Car policy : Car allowance Benefits : Pension (9% employer contribution), life assurance, private medical cover (following probationary period), gym membership

jobs.title: Territory Manager – X-Ray
jobs.description: Location: South West and Midlands Product: X-Ray capital equipment portfolio (mobile and fixed x-ray machines, including some dental x-ray machines) Who you’ll be working for: You will be working for a leading medical imaging equipment supplier serving healthcare providers throughout Ireland and the United Kingdom. Since 1967 they have provided innovative medical imaging technology, supported by a nationwide team of highly trained engineers and clinical applications specialists. As part of a larger group, the company also benefits from the scale and resources of an organisation comprising of 450+ healthcare industry specialists throughout the United Kingdom and Ireland. They inspire and motivate their employees to act on improving patient outcomes by delivering the best and most innovative healthcare products to clinicians and caregivers. What you’ll enjoy: Competitive salary and bonus structure Employee Assistance Program Educational Assistance Access to a training academy Enhanced annual and life leave Supportive colleagues to learn from and enjoy company social outings, parties, and events What you’ll be doing: Develop and manage modality sales opportunities and strategic reference sites in the assigned territory and other accounts as directed by your line manager. Develop new, profitable, and strategic business for the company in line with the agreed business targets set for all current product modalities. Promote the company (its features, advantages, benefits) to all existing installed base accounts and new potential customers. By active ‘account ownership,’ be the company representative in all aspects of corporate involvement within the Territory. Work under general ‘remote’ supervision whilst exercising independent judgment, functioning within approved guidelines. Stakeholders/Selling to: Primarily NHS Supply chain personnel, Procurements, Private Hospitals Finance Managers & some Dental Hospitals. Here’s what you need: You will have either previous capital sales experience or have worked in a clinical applications/clinical specialist related role in or related to Radiography/X-Ray or be a related clinician looking to move in to a more commercial role. Any experience from working in the radiology and/or vascular interventional care sectors would be advantageous but not essential. Basic Salary: £44,000 - £50,000 Bonus : £20,000 Car policy: Tesla 3 Benefits: Employee Events – Various events hosted throughout the year for all employees. Volunteer days and company sponsorship support for a charity of your choice. Financial Wellbeing – Free financial advice through a benefits broker, plus a Salary & Bonus exchange scheme to help with retirement planning. Finders Fee – £2,000 referral fee for recommending talented and motivated people who would be a good fit for the company. Employees of the Quarter – Recognition programme rewarding employees for excellence, with the chance to win a cash voucher. Savings Scheme – Set aside a fixed monthly amount from January to October, ready to access in November for Christmas. Enhanced Family Leave – Comprehensive leave covering Maternity, Paternity, Parental and Bereavement Leave. Enhanced Annual Leave – 25 days' annual leave, increasing regularly after five years' service up to 30 days per year. Enhanced Sick Leave – Increased paid sick leave as your length of service grows. Wellbeing – Externally trained Mental Health First Aiders, confidential 24/7 EAP mental health support for employees and their household, plus flu/hepatitis B vaccination costs covered. Eye Tests/Glasses – Full cost of an eye test every two years, plus an additional £70 towards eyewear. Cycle Scheme – Cycle to Work Scheme to support active travel and wellbeing. PHI Scheme – Permanent Health Insurance providing support if you're unable to work due to illness or injury. Pension – 5% employer pension contribution, rather than the legal minimum of 4%. Life Assurance – Four times your annual salary paid to your nominated person(s) in the event of your death. Long Service Awards – A special gift for every five years of employment. £5 lunch allowance

jobs.title: Territory Manager - Critical Care
jobs.description: Location: Wales, South Midlands, South West including Bournemouth Product: Ventilators (neonatal and adult), Temperature Management devices, Nebulisers Who you’ll be working for: Established in 2003, you will be joining one of the largest privately owned healthcare companies in Western Europe who have become a leading provider to all healthcare institutions with an expert team and an in-depth knowledge of the healthcare market. Their vision is to become a pan-European organisation with a reputation for exceeding their customers’ and their partners’ expectations. They inspire and motivate their employees to act on improving patient outcomes by delivering the best and most innovative healthcare products to clinicians and caregivers throughout Europe. They are constantly looking to expand, both in product portfolio and geographically. What you’ll enjoy: There is a good sales pipeline in place so good growth potential. You'll be launching a new product onto the market which will be a disruptor Lovely manager and close-knit fun team. The company is growing, so there are lots of opportunities to grow with it. There are 7 business units within the company, so scope to move around. People centered organsiation-they care about employee well being. What you’ll be doing: You'll provide procedural and product expertise to targeted customers and Key Opinion Leaders (KOL) through field travel, meeting attendance, educational seminars, and/or case observations. You will manage all aspects of business in the field. You will be responsible for the education of Anaesthetists, Intensivists and Nursing personnel on procedures and product applications and develop and support strong clinical relationships. jobs.title: Business Development Manager – Healthcare&Assistive Technology
jobs.description: Business Development Manager – Healthcare & Assistive Technology North of England | £50,000-£55,000 basic salary (flexible up to £60,000 for an exceptional candidate) | Uncapped quarterly commission | Annual performance bonus | Company car Established expertise. Exciting innovation. Serious growth ambitions. We’re looking for a Business Development Manager who knows how to open doors, build relationships and turn opportunities into business. An established, independent UK manufacturer and supplier of specialist technology solutions across healthcare, social care, disability services and independent living. With decades of experience in Environmental Control Systems (ECS), Technology Enabled Care (TEC) and Assisted Living, the business has built a strong reputation for delivering practical, innovative solutions that support independence, safety and quality of life. And they’re entering an exciting new phase of growth. With significant new technologies coming to market, including developments in proactive and preventative solutions, the business is expanding its opportunities across existing and emerging markets. These innovations have the potential to help organisations identify risks earlier, support more timely interventions and rethink how technology can contribute to better outcomes. Now they need someone with the commercial ambition to turn that potential into business. The opportunity This isn’t a role for someone who wants to inherit a territory and wait for orders. We’re looking for someone who can grow it. As Business Development Manager for the North of England, you’ll take ownership of a significant geographical territory, developing new business opportunities while building and strengthening relationships with existing customers. You’ll work across a diverse customer base, including: NHS organisations and healthcare providers Local authorities, commissioners and procurement teams Social care and supported living providers Specialist disability and rehabilitation services Housing organisations and technology-enabled care providers You’ll be introducing an established portfolio of specialist technology alongside exciting new solutions, helping customers understand how technology can address their challenges while delivering measurable benefits. From initial conversations and product demonstrations through to complex procurement processes and long-term partnerships, you’ll be responsible for turning opportunities into sustainable revenue. And you won’t be doing it alone. You’ll have the support of experienced technical, engineering, customer service and commercial colleagues. What you’ll be doing Winning new business: Identifying, developing and converting opportunities across healthcare, social care, disability services and related markets. Growing your territory: Creating and delivering a regional business development plan, identifying priority accounts and new market opportunities. Building influential relationships: Engaging with commissioners, senior decision-makers, clinicians, Occupational Therapists, procurement teams and service providers. Selling solutions, not just products: Understanding customer challenges and working with technical specialists to develop appropriate, commercially viable solutions. Developing existing accounts: Identifying opportunities to grow customer relationships, increase revenue and build long-term partnerships. Owning your pipeline: Managing opportunities from initial engagement through to conversion, with accurate forecasting and clear accountability for revenue and margin targets. Representing the business: Attending customer meetings, industry events, exhibitions and educational sessions to develop awareness and generate opportunities. What we’re looking for First and foremost, we want a successful business developer. Someone who can demonstrate a track record of generating new business, developing customer relationships and delivering commercial results. You’ll ideally bring: Proven success in a field-based B2B business development role, with evidence of achieving or exceeding sales targets. Experience selling products, technology or complex solutions into healthcare, social care, local authorities, the NHS or closely related sectors. The confidence and credibility to engage multiple stakeholders, including senior decision-makers. Strong commercial awareness, including pricing, margins, procurement processes and contract negotiations. Experience developing a territory, managing a sales pipeline and converting opportunities into revenue. Excellent communication, presentation and relationship-building skills. A proactive, resilient and self-motivated approach, with the drive to create opportunities rather than wait for them. Experience within Technology Enabled Care, assistive technology, healthcare technology, medical devices, nurse call or environmental controls would be advantageous. But you don’t need to know every product or technology from day one. What matters most is your ability to understand customer needs, recognise commercial opportunities, build trust and win business. Why join? Because this is an opportunity to make your mark. You’ll be joining a well-established UK business with ambitious growth plans, a developing sales team and an exciting portfolio of established and emerging technologies. The business combines the expertise and reputation of an established manufacturer with the flexibility and personal approach of an independent company. You’ll benefit from: The autonomy to develop and grow your own territory. An established product portfolio with exciting new innovations coming to market. Opportunities to develop new customers, markets and strategic partnerships. Direct access to senior leadership and the opportunity to influence commercial growth. Experienced technical and operational teams to support your sales activity. A collaborative, supportive culture where your contribution makes a visible difference. The package
